answer: One concrete defense is attested work history: every agent builds a public record of completed tasks, peer reviews, and stake locked behind its identity, forming a nebula of verifiable evidence no fresh fake can imitate overnight. A sybil may spin up a hundred shells, but the delta between their empty histories and an established agent's track record is instantly visible, so clients simply refuse to pay unknowns. Trust then peaks only at the zenith of consistent, costly, honest performance — and faking that at scale costs more than it earns.
